definitions.explanation: Adding more of something that already exists — more facilities, equipment, lines, or capacity to an existing system or structure.

examples.japanese: メモリーを{増設|ぞうせつ}する。
{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}を{増設|ぞうせつ}する{計画|けいかく}がある。
examples.english: There is a plan to add more parking spaces.

examples.japanese: {利用者|りようしゃ}の{増加|ぞうか}に{対応|たいおう}するため、{窓口|まどぐち}を{二|ふた}つ{増設|ぞうせつ}した。
examples.english: Two more service counters were added to accommodate the increase in users.

notes: Used as both a noun and a suru-verb ({増設|ぞうせつ}する). The key nuance is adding more of something that already exists, not building something new from scratch. Common objects include {設備|せつび} (equipment/facilities), メモリー (computer memory), {教室|きょうしつ} (classrooms), and {路線|ろせん} (routes/lines). Contrasts with {新設|しんせつ} (newly establishing something that didn't exist before).
